subject: history_social
passage: The Inca Empire, which stretched along the Andes Mountains of South America in the 1400s and 1500s, had no horses or wheeled vehicles for carrying messages. Instead, it relied on chasquis, runners stationed at posts along its roads. Each runner carried a message only a short distance before handing it to a fresh runner waiting at the next post. Because no single runner had to cover the whole route, messages could ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: be carried on horseback along the empire's flatter stretches of road.
choices.B: travel long distances much faster than one tired runner could carry them.
choices.C: reach distant cities only after long delays caused by exhausted runners.
choices.D: be written down so that runners would not have to remember them.

explanation.why: Each runner covered only a short stretch and then passed the message to a rested runner. Since nobody had to run the whole way and grow tired, the message could keep moving at a fast pace over long distances.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says the empire had no horses for carrying messages.
explanation.B: Correct. Handing the message to a fresh runner at each post keeps it moving quickly, which one runner could not do over a long route.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The relay system avoided exhausted runners, so it would reduce delays rather than cause them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says nothing about writing messages down or about runners' memory.
